subsystem.name: measurement
subsystem.note: The G6 harness, interlock tests/measurement, 14 files. One ledger per source file. provenance is the ninth file of this lane. It was blocked for most of the belt not by its own imports -- provenance.py needs no ai_invocation module, only the table -- but by its TESTS: the shared populate() helper seeds one invocation through ai_invocation.start_invocation, and 51 of the 61 cases depend on it. The operator ruled on 2026-08-22 that the lane would wait for that module rather than hand-write the row (the flagship fingerprint case is explicitly written through the real writer, and a hand-built row would leave 49 cases green over rows nobody writes).

systematic_mappings.why: The convention every module of this lane uses. readOnlyMap preserves insertion order, which asMapping depends on: section 6 orders the homogeneity verdict first so a reader who stops after the first screen does not stop before it.
systematic_mappings.affects: every entry that reads a header field

systematic_mappings.from: json.dumps(..., indent=2, ensure_ascii=True) and str(value) in a table cell
systematic_mappings.to: a renderer in this module, built on pythonJsonString
systematic_mappings.why: JSON.stringify is not json.dumps: it escapes no non-ASCII and it prints an integral float as an integer. Both differences are invisible to any assertion that parses the text, which is D-0017 rule 4's argument for the control plane's persisted JSON applied to a rendered one. pythonJsonString is the existing one-renderer-per-behaviour helper.

systematic_mappings.from: repr(value) for a REAL column, and json.dumps of coverage.ratio
systematic_mappings.why: Python and JavaScript disagree on three things about a float: the .0 on an integral value, the magnitude at which exponential notation starts (1e16/1e-4 against 1e21/1e-7), and the two-digit signed exponent. All three reach the digest or the header. New oracle face, same shape as the fixed-format one (D-0104).
systematic_mappings.affects: the fingerprint entries and the rendering entries

systematic_mappings.to: safeIntegers(true) on the fingerprint's row statement
systematic_mappings.why: Python's sqlite3 returns an int for INTEGER and a float for REAL, so isinstance separates them. better-sqlite3 returns a JavaScript number for both, so 1 and 1.0 would hash alike -- collapsing the distinction the type tag exists to make. safeIntegers returns every INTEGER as a BigInt, which restores the five-way split and also keeps the digest exact past 2^53 (D-0007). The SQL text is unchanged.

systematic_mappings.to: src/about.ts TOOL_VERSION, pinned to package.json by a target-only case
systematic_mappings.why: The source reads one literal so a build cannot report a version it is not. This port has two places a version can live, and a runtime read of package.json resolves differently from src/ and dist/ -- so the literal is pinned by a test instead, which keeps the single-source-of-truth property without a path that can be wrong in the installed build.

systematic_mappings.from: pytest's `db` fixture and try/finally connection pairs
systematic_mappings.to: a per-test productionDb() plus withWritable / withMeasurement (rule 8)
systematic_mappings.why: The convention every measurement test file in this port uses.
systematic_mappings.affects: every entry that touches a database

systematic_mappings.why: Raised by the codex review gate: `.all()` would hold every row of a cumulatively-growing table in the heap before the first byte is hashed, which is a resource behaviour the port would not share with the thing it ports. The digest is unchanged -- same statement, same order, same values.

target_only_tests.note: Target-only tests translate no source case and are NOT counted as ported coverage. Four pin PORT DIVERGENCES this port had to design around -- the version literal, an integral float rendering as 1.0 rather than 1, an INTEGER hashing apart from the REAL that equals it, and a digest that stays exact past 2^53 -- and none of them has a source case because none of the three underlying differences exists in Python. The other eight close gaps a 37-mutation sweep found, all INHERITED: each mutation was applied to interlock's own provenance.py at 65f36c5 and its 61 cases stayed green (measured, not inferred). Each is recorded with its verdict under mutation_sweep and each was confirmed to kill its mutation and only its mutation. A thirteenth was added after the codex review gate found two exported frozen types adopting the caller's Map instead of copying it: Python's frozen dataclasses do the same and its factory is the only constructor the source uses, so nothing upstream notices, but both types are exported here and a caller holding that Map could change the rendered query text after the digest was computed. Further cases were added by the D-0109 / D-0110 remediation belt, which repaired defects this ledger had disclosed (and, in four modules, defects it had not): each is the evidence for a divergence recorded above.

notes_on_exports.what: The barrel exposes provenance's PeriodRefused as ReportPeriodRefused.
notes_on_exports.why: windows.ts exports a PeriodRefused too, and they are two different classes in interlock as well -- one refuses a report period, the other an observation period. Python namespaces them per module; a flat barrel cannot, so the newcomer is qualified and each module still exports the bare name under its own path.

notes_on_exports.what: TOOL_VERSION is exported from src/about.ts and re-exported through provenance.ts and both barrels.
notes_on_exports.why: The source's __all__ carries TOOL_VERSION on the provenance module for the same reason: a consumer checking which build produced a report should not have to know which module the literal lives in.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: An aggregate-mode fingerprint cannot distinguish two reads that differ only by an in-place UPDATE, and a report can be generated in that mode.
inherited_limitations.note: Deliberate and reproduced exactly, including the demonstration: one ported case asserts the content digest MOVES on a usage_status backfill and its twin asserts the aggregate digest does NOT. The mode carries AGGREGATE_STATEMENT into both renderings so a report produced that way says in terms that its fingerprint does not establish identity of content.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere; the weaker mode is section 6's own rejected form, kept reachable and labelled.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: iso8601Ms refuses an instant past 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z with a PeriodRefused, where Python raises OverflowError from datetime's own ceiling.
inherited_limitations.note: A disclosed divergence in the refusal TYPE, not in what is accepted: both stop, at the same instant, and neither renders a header. The source's failure escapes the ControlPlaneRefusal family and arrives as an arithmetic error with no explanation; this port keeps it inside the family the caller is already catching and says what the limit is. No ported case reaches it.
inherited_limitations.where_a_fix_belongs: upstream, if interlock ever wants that boundary inside its refusal hierarchy.

entries.reason: Deferred from the provenance belt and landed with ac9, which is where the thing it integrates with lives. It is an INTEGRATION case -- it builds a cohort with selectCohort, measures it with measureAc9, and asserts that coverageFromAc9 and imputationFromAc9 copy that report's own numbers rather than recounting them -- so porting it before ac9 existed would have asserted that the adapters copy numbers the test made up. Accounted for here, where its source file is; its target lives in test/measurement/ac9.test.ts.

mutation_sweep.ran: 37 mutations, one per property the ported cases claim to pin, 2026-08-22

survivors.mutation: the fingerprint default flips from content to aggregate
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Every case on both sides passes the mode explicitly, so the default is unexercised. Section 6 makes the strong mode the default precisely so a caller who did not know there was a choice does not publish the weaker claim.

survivors.mutation: the absent-table check is removed from _columns_of
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The empty-columns backstop then refuses instead, with the same type and also naming the table, so the ported case passes either way on both sides. The two sentences tell an operator different things -- a typo in the table list, or a table that exists and is somehow shapeless -- so the new case asserts which one was said.

survivors.mutation: the column names are not fed to the hasher
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: No case on either side changes a table's shape. The source's reason is a schema change under a report's feet: the digest must move even where no row moved. The new case adds a column to an EMPTY table, so the shape is the only thing that changed.

survivors.mutation: the length prefix is dropped from _feed, keeping the delimiter
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: The ported boundary case pins the SEPARATOR rather than the length: with the delimiter kept, ('as','b') and ('a','sb') still hash apart, so the case passes on both sides against an encoding that is only conditionally injective. Dropping the delimiter too IS caught by it -- measured. The new case is a pair the delimiter alone cannot separate: a value containing the delimiter sequence, where ('x','ys:z') and ('xs:y','z') spell one stream.

survivors.mutation: rows are ordered by rowid instead of by every column
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: No case on either side holds two rows whose rowid order differs from their column order. The source's reason is a VACUUM: it renumbers rowids and changes nothing a report can read, so a digest that moved for it would cry wolf at exactly the reader trying to establish that two reads agree. The new case inserts the same two rows in the two orders and asserts one digest.

survivors.mutation: aggregate mode always uses MAX(rowid), never MAX(seq)
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: None of the three tables every ported case fingerprints has a seq column, on either side, so the branch is unreachable from the suite. The new case builds a table where the two maxima differ and moves only seq.

survivors.mutation: an empty schema_migration ledger is accepted
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Unreachable through the real opener on both sides. The new case builds the state by hand rather than by emptying a real ledger -- the production schema has a trigger saying a migration record is never deleted, and defeating it would be testing against a database the schema forbids.

survivors.mutation: the JSON rendering stops escaping non-ASCII
survivors.verdict: inherited blind spot, closed with a target-only test
survivors.note: Every case on both sides is ASCII, including the cp932 case that looks like it covers this -- it asserts over ASCII inputs. A query name or text is caller-supplied and this organization writes prose in Japanese; a raw character there crashes the report on the console section 6 says it is printed to. The new case also asserts the text survives a round trip, so the escaping is a rendering choice and not a change to what the report says it ran.

mutation_sweep.note: All eight survivors were re-run against the new target-only cases and each is now killed by its own case and no other. The length-prefix entry above corrects a weaker first mutation of mine: dropping only the digits left the delimiter in place, and the delimiter alone is what the ported case actually pins.

divergences.behaviour: ImputationRule carries unconfirmedResponseCount as well as unboundedMissing, its supportsAcceptanceClaim requires both to be zero, and the header prints the new count. interlock's header carries only unboundedMissing.
divergences.note: An INHERITED DEFECT in interlock, fixed here on the operator's ruling of 2026-08-22 rather than reproduced. interlock's Ac9Report disqualifies on two populations and its header on one, so over a report containing an unfinished invocation the AC-9 section says the claim is unsupported and the header says it is supported -- and render.py puts both answers in ONE document (.header.imputation_rule.supports_acceptance_claim true, .sections.ac9.facts.imputation.supports_acceptance_claim false), measured against interlock at 65f36c5, not inferred. The lane's own recommendation was reproduce-and-disclose, consistent with the shadow caveat and the provenance ORDER BY tie; the operator overrode it because those are omissions a reader can work around and this is a document asserting both true and false about one claim. interlock is frozen, so no upstream fix is coming: this is PERMANENT and continuo is authoritative.
divergences.parity_cost: continuo's rendered report differs from interlock's for any period containing an unfinished invocation: the header gains an imputation_rule.unconfirmed_response_count key and imputation_rule.supports_acceptance_claim flips to false. interlock#74 AC3 compares these documents, so this is the one place the two are intended to disagree, and it is reachable from this ledger. The constructor's arity also diverges: unconfirmedResponseCount is REQUIRED, with no default, because an optional count falling back to zero would leave a public construction path producing the very contradiction the decision removes. Four ported cases in this file build an ImputationRule directly and now pass `unconfirmedResponseCount: 0`; the state they build and everything they assert is unchanged.
divergences.evidence: test/measurement/ac9.test.ts::a deliberate divergence from interlock (target-only) > the header's acceptance predicate agrees with the report's
divergences.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere; interlock is frozen and continuo is the authority for this field.

divergences.behaviour: renderHeaderMarkdown escapes non-ASCII in a cell AND escapes the dotted field name the same way it escapes a value. interlock escapes a pipe and a newline in a value only, and interpolates the field name raw.
divergences.note: Disclosed on this belt under D-0022 and repaired on that rule's withdrawal. A dotted field name is built from map KEYS -- a query name, an exclusion reason, an unmatched-bucket name -- so a key carrying a pipe shifts every value after it one column left and one carrying a newline ends the row. The JSON rendering has been ASCII-safe from the start (ensure_ascii); this makes the Markdown one match, so both renderings honour the claim their docstrings make. The escaping was verified the way lane C's 'green guarantees nothing' note asks: the reportValue call was reverted at this site and the case above was confirmed to fail FOR THAT REASON. Three of the ten sites checked that way were initially passing for a different reason and were rewritten before this belt shipped.
divergences.parity_cost: continuo's Markdown header differs from interlock's wherever a value or a key is not printable ASCII. The JSON rendering is unchanged.
divergences.evidence: test/measurement/provenance.test.ts::deliberate divergences from interlock (target-only) > the Markdown rendering escapes a value and a field name the console cannot take
divergences.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere; interlock is frozen and continuo is the authority for this renderer.

divergences.behaviour: The content fingerprint orders rows by every column AND by each column's storage class (typeof). interlock orders by the columns alone.
divergences.note: Disclosed on this belt under D-0022 and repaired on that rule's withdrawal. SQLite's ORDER BY compares INTEGER 1 and REAL 1.0 as EQUAL while feedValue hashes them apart, so the source's ordering is not a total order over the values it hashes and two databases holding identical content produce two digests -- the one claim the field makes. typeof() separates only rows the value comparison left equal, so no other digest moves. The earlier disclosure argued that a tie-breaker would move continuo's digests away from interlock's; it moves them only for tables containing such a tie, and for those the interlock digest is not a function of content in the first place.
divergences.parity_cost: A digest over a table holding a cross-storage-class tie differs from interlock's. Every other digest is unchanged.
divergences.evidence: test/measurement/provenance.test.ts::deliberate divergences from interlock (target-only) > the digest does not move when two rows tie across storage classes
divergences.where_a_fix_belongs: nowhere; interlock is frozen and continuo is the authority for this digest.
